name: Icovellauna

attributes.attribute: a Continental Celtic goddess with inscriptions at Metz and Trier
likely a water and healing goddess, with an eight-sided shrine at the Spring of Sablo

sources: Green, Miranda. Symbol and Image in Celtic Religious Art. London: Routledge, 1989, 40.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Icovellauna is a Continental Celtic goddess. Inscriptions to her have been found at Metz and Trier in Germany. Little is known about her meaning or cult. The first syllable of her name, Ico- , means water. She is presumably a water divinity. She is probably the healing goddess. Her eight-sided shrine was excavated at the Spring of Sablon.

okr.objective: Document the Continental Celtic goddess Icovellauna and her inscriptions.
key_results: Record the inscriptions at Metz and Trier.
Note the water meaning of the Ico- syllable.
Note the eight-sided shrine at the Spring of Sablon.
